HG16-refix:
De-hypnosis: wake up inside the influence

One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is influence literacy: an increased awareness of all the ways your attention is being shaped in your day-to-day life. By a screen? By a specific ad? By a politician? By religious fear? By erotic imprinting? By charismatic authority? By pressure to belong? By shame? By a sense of urgency? By repetition? It’s all around you. Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.

You are likely being manipulated if you feel any of the following; urgency, you are special, FOMO (fear of missing out), not be included, sexual charge, shame, confused, someone will rescue you, destiny, you should obey, secret knowledge, and an excessive sense of certainty about something way too quickly and you have a sense that one good question will break the spell.

First of all, if you sense you are being hypnotically influenced, stop. Don’t obey, but don’t rebel, just realise that you are being influenced.

Secondly, some of the ways that hypnotic language is used to manipulate are where you have consented to something you didn’t realise, or you being given only one choice, or something not yet agreed upon is embedded in a sentence. For example;

You will soon realise that I am right …. Or you may, in time, decide to admit that …. Or the only reason you do not agree is …. Or part of you already knows …. Or your higher self wants …. Or everyone who is awake knows …. Or the reason you do not believe that is true is because your ego does not want you to …

If you are unsure, you may like to ask yourself the following questions;

What am I being asked to agree to? What choice am I being given? What is being assumed that I may not agree with? Who benefits if I comply? What is the emotionally charged part of what is being said? What is not being said? If I say no, what will the consequences be? (Will I be punished, shamed, laughed at, not be included, be told I am not ‘awake’ etc?)

This is a good guide to help engage your ‘adult’ in the conversation. The more powerful the ‘state’ the more you will need to make use of these.

Soft language can still take away choice

Be aware that even when using ‘permissive’ language, you can still take away choice. Be aware of;

Indirect suggestions are a very effective way to by-pass the subject’s ‘skeptical guard’. They do this by not directly telling the subject what to do. This does not mean that indirect suggestions are not specific. It simply means that they are worded in a vague, conversational, suggestive manner.

1) Utilizing induction techniques while seemingly explaining something (even something like "anti hypnosis" can use the same mechanics of induction).

2) In any way making it so that whatever the subject says, shows that a suggestion has worked, when this may not be the case (this includes answering yes, no, noticing something, not noticing something, trying not to do something, not answering, etc etc etc)

3) Including phrases such as whether or not you notice etc etc

4) Including any concepts that may make a subject think they must obey, or take on a role, or that it is good/safe to please the guide or belong to someone etc etc.

5) Fractionating a subject without telling them that you are going to take them in and out of absorption a few times.

6) Giving a subject cues (words, gestures, blinks, sounds, listening a certain number of times etc) that you intend to use to make them do something at a later date, without informing them exactly what it is that they will be doing.

7) Including suggestions for amnesia, or making a subject think that something (dream, amnesia, imagery, body experiences etc) has happened when this may not necessarily be the case.

8) Not taking a subject out at the end of a recording, or leaving them with a role to play, with their judgement down, with their physical abilities down, with their minds blank, or in any other way different for an indefinite length of time.

In order for a subject to be making a REAL choice whilst in a hypnosis, there MUST be at least one way for a subject NOT to carry on with the hypnosis if they wish. This could be by making the hypnosis lighter, using a different method of hypnosis, being in full awareness whilst in a hypnosis, or being able to pause or stop the hypnosis. Just so you know, if you say no, you are quite entitled to mean NO, even if someone with a nice voice is asking you to do something! Also, just because you don't say anything, or don't know what to say, DOES NOT mean yes!

(see appendix C for a longer version of the de hypno)
HG17-refix:
Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

Hypnotic inductions are intended to bring your attention together so that you can hear some material that you might not hear when you are sober. It is not intended as a place where you surrender yourself, or go to sleep, or need to obey anyone. Sometimes if you are sober and finding it hard to focus because you are distracted or too analytical or putting up with resistance to working on something, an induction can be useful. However if you are already pretty trancey (because you have meditated before hand, or because you are drunk on loveyhuasca or doing lucid dreaming or working on grief or listening to music or praying or tired or whatever) you might want to skip to orienting yourself and making sure you are contained before you go any further.

If you do want to induce a trance make it as deep as you need it to be for you to be able to be focussed, warm, receptive, embodied and able to stop when you need to. It doesn't have to be very deep at all.

What an induction is actually doing

It's preparation, gathering up your attention, sometimes it's deepening too. It will work better if you make it fit to what comes up for you. Counting is one way of gathering up your attention. You can also do it through talking, or telling a story, or movement, or sound, or encouraging you to be curious about something. If you do it through any of these means, say so. Just because it's done elegantly, doesn't mean it has to be covert.

It may be a good idea to try out the suggestion you are going to make on a simple target, to see if it works for you, before you go to the trouble of deepening. If you have already got what you want, you can always develop a more receptive response to it afterwards, you don't need all the ceremony to make it happen.

Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance

Decide what you are going to do, and how you are going to anchor it at the beginning, and how you are going to get back. Do you want it to be warm or firm or directed or neutral or what? Don't use floating and going down stairs and going through gardens and going to inner places and seeing a colour and talking to a child inside, even if they all appeal to you! If you need to change metaphors, do it consciously.

It is OK to do this with no imagery, you will get the signal some other way. Try and make the language you use for counting in etc match the world you have chosen. Come back out again by reversing the journey in some way. It is ok to borrow qualities, but don't be somebody else.

Try and restrict yourself to one key verb, or a particular sense quality, or a small bit of text you repeat to yourself, or something, to get you from one bit to the next. Read it out loud before you start. Long beautiful sentences often turn to soup in an induction.

Before you begin

Before you start:

Read this induction. Come all the way back again while you are reading it. Decide what it is you want to explore, what it is you want to leave alone, how much time you have. Maybe you just want to explore having more love or play or confidence or creativity or communion or whatever, you don't have to find a problem. Make sure you have enough time to come back out again and think about it.

Make sure you are safe. Don't do this if you are driving or near water or playing with machinery or around people you need to look after. Don't do this if you are intoxicated or in any state where you might be acutely confused or unable to look after yourself - in that case you need immediate support, not exploratory hypnosis. (But see the bit above about already being open, as this is not talking about deepening when unstable).

Practise First decide on how spacious, or how firmly inviting you wish to be. Let yourself know that you will need to close your eyes, and that you may need to come out a few times, as well as coming out at the end. If you are going to record the exercise, it may be a good idea to read the script first, if possible. Remind yourself that you can always stop the exercise by saying 'stop', or 'less', or 'quiet'. Remind yourself that you can always come out simply by opening your eyes, that you do not need to get everyone's agreement inside to finish.

It is wise, until you are fully confident about coming in and out, to practise in a context where you do not need to draw on your maximum efforts. Once you know how to change direction, you will not need to supervise all the time. Your response will get easier, and less effortful. A 'no' is a 'no' and silence does not give anyone the right to add to what is not there.

You will need to develop the next part of your induction, based on what you do get. This is the principle of utilizing what you do get, and it may change what you get. If you don't get anything, then you don't get anything! Remember that you need to lay out for yourself the instructions for safety and for coming out. You will learn more about the language you can use in Appendix B. And you will learn how to use them, once the induction is over, in Let the next response guide you .

Sober induction: 3–5 minutes

Practise reading this slowly either into a recorder, or reading it aloud, or even learn it so that you can use it in silence. Choose to use one of the three anchors (sound, bodily contact or two hands) throughout, and use the opening phrase of your choice. Each time that 'the anchor' is mentioned in the script below, use the one that you have chosen. Pause at the end of each paragraph for a few moments. Don't read aloud the instructions to yourself about how to read it.

You might let your eyes settle somewhere in the room,

then notice the surface you are sitting (lying) on, and notice the feel of that contact, and as you notice the feel of that contact, you might notice a sound, or your own breathing,

There's all the time in the world to do this.

You may notice a thought about what has happened today, or perhaps a thought about doing this, but even if there is a thought there, you can turn your attention to the anchor,

and as you turn your attention to the anchor, you might notice something about it that interests you. Maybe it's something about the sound, or something about the contact, or even something about the way you listen,

And you might give yourself the time to notice this, just as you might give someone dear to you time to speak.

Think of a good phrase for this exercise and say it.

Feel free to close your eyes, soften them or keep them open as you go through these steps.

Count from 5 to 1, slowly.

5. Bring to mind something you want to find. 4. Focus on what you find. 3. Take a little break after the words. 2. Listen to this break. 1. Stay with it for a minute.

Bring the thing you chose to think about to mind. If you don’t want to do that, stay with the contact you made.

Now, what do you notice?

Give yourself time to notice whatever comes to you, sensations, words, images, feelings, movements etc.

Give yourself time to notice what is coming to you, whether it has words or not.

Already open? Contain before you deepen

Use this when you are already open, to contain your state.

This is good when you are already opening a state, via loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, erotic energy, exhaustion, being overwhelmed by beauty, etc. You want to stabilize your state before opening it more strongly.

I already have this state open. I don’t want to open it more strongly. I want to aim it, stabilize it and keep it kind.

Look around you. Tell yourself where you are. Tell yourself the date, or at least the day. Feel your feet, hands and spine. Get a sense of yourself. Then focus on the physical sensations in your thumbs as you push them into your index fingers. Really feel the friction.

I will only allow myself to go as far as I can integrate. Too much can wait. My body will be safe. My adult self is here. My child doesn’t have to do this alone.

When you are oriented, say: “Please show me the next thing I need to know, whether it is a truth, a symbol, a feeling, a question or an action I need to take.”

Stay awake when your mind likes to escape

Do this sitting up, with your eyes open, feeling your feet and breathing naturally.

I am not going to go away. I am going to come here more.

Look at an object. Feel your spine.

Ask yourself if you are daydreaming to get guidance or digest emotional things, or if you are escaping.

Ask for help with whatever it is: seeing what you need to do if it is guidance, or coming into the present and seeing what you are avoiding if it is avoidance.

If you find that whenever you are still, you escape into sleepiness and diffuse states, do this exercise to increase your ability to be alert instead of relaxed. Do it with your eyes open, moving your hands. Do it for a while, and then stop it deliberately so you can see what is there without escaping.

Do this with your eyes open. Push your thumb and forefinger together gently and let go a few times, becoming more clear and alert each time. Then deliberately stop and notice what happens in the first second after you stop, whether there is an echo or not. Keep yourself up and work at this level.

Quick Inductions and Triggers: At your service.

2-hand induction:

The two-hand induction

Mind if I borrow your hands for a moment? Just for a second, put one hand on your heart, and one on your solar plexis. The one on your heart is your nurturer, the one on your solar plexis is your vulnerable child. Now just breathe gently and tell yourself, "the love is above, the child is below, and the adult is present." Tell yourself, "I will send love to the child, and I will receive the child's signal. Then I will send love again, and I will listen again."

Sleep induction

Sleep induction:

This induction is different, because all other inductions get you back to your adult so you can write and do stuff, and this one is going to put you to sleep so analysis can get off duty and let revelation do its thing. Try out Nimja's sleep playlist here .

Optional fractionation: practice coming back

Fractionation (optional):

As long as you are open about using it, fractionation is OK.

"Open your eyes and come back, feel yourself in the room. If you want to come out of hypnosis, that's OK. But you might want to try something: close (or soften) your eyes and see if you can go back in. Remember, you can always choose to stop."

Deepening (optional):

If it is useful for you, you can go deeper into absorption. But if it isn't useful, you're already awake enough.

Deepening, if useful

Take yourself to your room in your heart, your garden or temple of inner peace, sit next to a fire with your Protector, float on a lake, sit in a chair where an adult waits for you, etc, etc, etc. Just pick one.

And see who wants to talk to you first.

Trance (optional):

Optional trance depth check

Give yourself permission to not have to do anything.

"If it is useful, my wise subconscious may cause one of my fingers to twitch, or pulse, or lift up, or get warm, or tingly, or whatever, to let me know that I am ready to meet with whomever wants to see me in my inner space." And of course you're not going to make it happen, or pretend it is happening, you're just going to wait in love.

It doesn't mean that anything will happen, but if something happens with one of your fingers, or you feel some other bodily change, none of it proves truth; at most, something may be listening.

A shortcut back into hypnosis

Once you've learned a useful induction and also the full return below, you can make up your own shortcut for getting back under hypnosis. My dad used to do a mudra (hand sign) by bringing two fingers together in an "okay" sign, and it would help him relax. He even did it while driving, but that's his experience, not a recommendation to enter trance at the wheel. So keep the cue you use for calming yourself while alert separate from the one for going into inward hypnosis!

Choose a Unique Word, Phrase or Movement You may want to add a gesture, but it's not necessary. When you are in a familiar and welcome hypnotic state that you like - not at the height of an emotional experience, and not in a child state or with a traumatic scene - start to pair that state with that word, phrase or gesture. You are giving that word, phrase or gesture a meaning that you choose.

When you are in a place and time where you have set aside time and it is appropriate and you want to deliberately start hypnosis with your short cut, then you can return to this familiar way of listening, from where you can change the direction of your experience or end the hypnosis.

Return fully. When at another appropriate time you want to deliberately start practicing hypnosis, use your short cut. Give it time. You can start to make your longer induction shorter as you find that the short cut works, but if it doesn't work, you can always use the familiar induction. There is no set number of times that you need to do this, or that you need to be instantaneously really deep into hypnosis or experience a particular sensation, it is completely up to you.

First, is it useful? Will it be there when you want it to be, not there when you don't want it to be? Can you change direction and return when you want to? It shouldn't become obedience to a narrator, notification, or overheard word. Going in faster doesn't determine what material you can handle.

Never train, test, or use hypnotic re-entry while driving or anything where you need to be actively paying attention even if it is open eyed and even if the words are conditional.

And if you don't want to any more, just stop doing it, remove it from any recordings you are using, any active apps, use an induction you are familiar with and state that you are finished using it whilst awake. If this doesn't stop the association straight away, and you are still getting unwanted affects or feeling disorientated, seek qualified help to sort it out. Until the next time you want to do it, you should not use the trigger.
HG31-refix:
Appendix B: NLP without turning yourself into a sales seminar

You don’t have to know the terms to practice the core method. If you want to brush up on the art of imagery, bodily states, how to effectively rehearse new behaviors, how to choose more effective sentences to say to yourself, etc., then you might want to read this appendix. NLP is useful when it helps the system listen, but it’s easy to turn it into a bag of tricks and forget that love, truth, contact, and consent are essential.

The four NLP layers

First, it works on a Sensory Level of NLP: changing the form of an inner experience, where people see or hear an image, the distance or size or brightness, the volume of a sound, posture, pressure.

2. State Level of NLP – Help them to access a new state of warmth or adult’ness or whatever

3. Strategy level of NLP – Help them to re-practice a better strategy or ‘When the cue, the adult does this’

4. Language Level of NLP – Using the language of a gentle voice which paces what is already true, opens up awareness, presumes their ability to do something safe, links events in a good cause and effect way, embeds invitations or uses de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative and grandiose language

The Milton Model, minus the covert sales seminar

aka The Milton Model (minus the selling seminar covertly)

Have you ever had someone tell you to ‘Relax now’ or ‘Stop being anxious’ or said ‘Trust me’ and you thought to yourself NO F**KING WAY!

Well in this case we want to use ‘indirect’ language to help you get past the part that wants to argue with you and get to the place you want to be.

1. Start with what you know to be true, take the pressure off, presume what you know to be safe that they can do and invite them to do 1 thing:

2. As your body is noticing the bed beneath it, you can start to stop holding the day alone.

Here you have paced what is already real for them, opened up awareness, validated their reaction, presumed their capacity to do something, used a bridge word and invited them to do just one thing and have a way to know if it is working in their body.

Pattern 1: Pacing and leading — truth before suggestion

Here is an example of pacing and leading when you are anxious.

It may be as simple as ‘Truth, Invite, Truth, Invite’ etc.

It is completely true that the sensation of ________ / emotion of _____ is coming up for me. It also makes sense that my system is trying to react to this by doing this/thinking ________. While that is completely true, there is another thing that is completely true and that is that my adult self is here breathing in this room right now and willing to listen to what is coming up next.

Pattern 2: Awareness verbs

‘Awareness’ verbs: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider

Pattern 3: Presuppositions

Warning!!! Use this powerful tool only to presume their choice to do something when it will occur and presume their ability to do something that you know will be good for them (being in a state of safety, love, adult leading etc)

Pattern 4: Gentle cause-effect bridges

As, while, because, when, after, before, which means etc.

In general the first statement is too strong because it is unlikely that the trauma will go away just by breathing. The second statement is more accurate because as you breathe you can get your adult self present to listen to what the wounded part needs.

Pattern 5: Embedded invitations

Here is an example of an embedded invitation.

Example: “And as you sit there, you may allow yourself to realise…”

Another example (directed to inner child parts): “And you may allow yourself to realise that….”

I am sure you get the idea. Try using one (but don’t go overboard – if you start rattling off ten of them in a row, it becomes pretty obvious that you went on a weekend certification course, yo).

Pattern 6: Ethical double binds

Maniplative double bind questions look like this:

Ethical double bind questions offer two ethically safe ways to move forward:

Pattern 7: Conversational postulates

Example: “Would you rather feel a warming sensation or an expansive sensation?”

An example of using a postulate as an invitation looks like this:

“Can I ask the system to take the next step without re-opening the wound?”

Pattern 8: Tag questions

Pattern 8: Tag questions (Is it? Cant it? Doesnt it? etc)

Works pretty much the same way as the above, but again can get a bit oily if you use it too often, so be sparing.

Pattern 9: Nominalizations

Pattern 9: Nominalisations (healing, safety, trust, integration, communion, clarity, rest etc)

Sometimes its useful to be vague about something so that the subconscious can fill in the blank with whatever will work best for them in a specific way.

Example: “And you may begin to feel more safety in whatever way is right for you.”

Pattern 10: Meta Model questions (The de-hypnosis tool)

Pattern 10: Meta Model questions — the de-hypnosis tool

To ‘Milton Model’ means to open things up, to ‘Meta Model’ means to ask “What do yo mean by that?” It is important to use both of these when working ethically with people.

“…How specifically? According to who? Compared to what? Are you saying Always? Never? What specifically will happen? How do I know? What evidence would I need to change my mind?”

So if I feel the body starting to stiffen up, I will ‘Milton’ it. If I feel I am eluding the truth, I will ‘Meta’ it.

Sensory, state, and strategy tools

Submodalities — editing the form, not denying the truth

Submodalities (Editing the truth without deleting it)

For this you need to have some sensory properties to work with. If the fear, craving, fantasy, belief, memory whatever, doesnt look or sound far or near, bright or dim, loud or quiet, fast or slow, inside or outside the body, heavy or light etc, then just dont use this tool.

“How is this represented, and how can I change its properties in a way that will serve me better?”

“I’m not deleting this signal, I’m just altering the volume so that I can hear it without being overwhelmed.”

(If you have a guard, its a good idea to ask them first if it’s ok to do this)

“Is it ok if I move the image a bit further away, or turn the volume of the voice down so that my adult self can be here and hear what you need to say to me?”

Anchoring (The back to hypnosis doorway)

Anchoring — giving the body a doorway back

There are many ways to do this. Put your hand on your heart, touch two fingers together, use a breath, a word, a particular body posture, smell, song, whatever. Feel something that you have got to in reality that you want to be able to get to easily when you need to. Do your anchor thing and say to yourself that this is available to you. Do make sure you do it when you have clearly got it. To get yourself back into a good hypnosis state easily, dont go for a peak state but for a good hypnotic state. See the main induction for a quick way to get back into hypnosis. Do make sure this is different from both your alert and calm cue and your synchronicity wake up cue.

Using synchronicity as your own wake-up bell

Using synchronicity (The synchronicity wake up cue)

People often ask what the synchronicity means. Sometimes they get a great insight from it, but other times they get obsessed trying to work out patterns etc. I am using the noticing of the synchronicity to WAKE UP.

It is my cue to:

Whenever I notice it I use it as a cue for waking up from whatever state I am in, feeling my body, feeling the room I'm in, remembering that what I'm noticing is not proof for what I'm interpreting from the coincidences, widening my state so that I can see beyond what my current state is showing me. I then look for the truth of what is going on (What is really going on, what is just my interpretation? What needs to be warmed? What needs to be protected? What action needs to be taken?) and I go into the highest state I can get into where I can objectively and clearly see what is going on from that situation from the highest perspective I can get to, whilst remaining in my body, not leaving the facts of the situation and not leaving my regular human state. From that state I feel my feelings. I look for the truth of the situation. If I am in a negative state, I check if it is a message from my Inner Child, my Protector or if I just need to grieve. I check if it is a message from my physical body (if there is a problem with my body that needs to be taken care of) or if there is something that needs to be done about the situation. From that place I choose what to do. I choose at least one thing to do that is from a loving place. I allow myself to be in whatever state is real for me, which now includes objectivity, clarity, ease, peace, freedom, joy, gratitude, etc.

In other words: Stop-orient-go wider-reality check-listen-do at least one thing from a loving place.

This way I don't go into identification but I still hear the message of the state if it's negative.

Installing the synchronicity cue

How to install Synchronicity cues:

Mentally rehearse the following: Imagine that you have noticed a synchronicity that is obviously harmless.

Feel the "whoa" of stimulation that you just got from noticing it.

Use that stimulation to feel your feet, your body, your breathing, your room.

Reiterate to yourself that whenever you notice a synchronicity, it is just a bell that rings to wake you up, it is not proof for what you are interpreting from it.

Ask yourself: "What does my Nurturer think about this?", "What does my Protector think about this?", "What does my Leader think about this?"

Rehearse going back to a more grounded state and to a more wide view of the situation.

Rehearse yourself taking at least one action. Rehearse yourself waking up completely.

Mind the caveats! You must be the one authoring these. You must see them. You can always undo them. You must use them only to help you orient. They do not authorize you to make a decision. They are not proof for what your intuition is telling you. They do not stop you from hearing the message of your intuition if it is warning you about something. You can't use them to control other people.

This is very similar to implementation intention . I'm not aware of research into implementation intention for this specific thing, but the general mechanisms appear to work; a paper explaining how and why they work can be found here .

A downside of synchronicity cues is that they can lead to false positives. We do this on purpose when we rehearse what to do when we notice a synchronicity (we create an association in our head); however, when you are absorbed in something and/or when you are destabilized, you might think that you saw a synchronicity when in fact there wasn't any. Research has shown that people that score high on apophenia tests also score high for detecting patterns that were not really there, as well as scoring high on psychosis spectrum traits [1, 2] (this is not saying that noticing patterns is bad; in fact, it's not a pathology).

If you feel that synchronicity cues are making these things worse (e.g. you feel like you have to look for them all the time, you can't sleep, you feel anxious, you are sure that random things happen in your life in order to tell you something, you can't tell the difference between noticing something and interpreting what it might mean, etc.), you should deactivate synchronicity cues.

You can do that by not rehearsing them anymore and by saying to yourself (when you are fully awake) that you don't want to use synchronicity as a cue anymore (e.g. "From now on, I am no longer going to use noticing synchronicity as a cue for waking up."). Remove it from your list of cues, so that you won't rehearse it anymore.

Reframing — changing the meaning without lying

In the past I used to reframe by telling myself that whatever problem I had was actually a good thing. However, that is not honest. Now I reframe by asking myself:

Perceptual positions — self, other, witness, universal heart

Here is a rough outline of the NLP tools and techniques I use:

Perceptual Positions : 1) seeing from Self, 2) then seeing from Other, 3) then seeing from Witness, and 4) then seeing from Universal Heart. I do this to see the situation with more accuracy.

I will not use this to rationalize bad behavior, but only to break out of a prison of perception.

Future pacing — let the future test the insight

Future Pacing : 1) Once I have seen the situation more clearly, I will imagine future scenarios where my old behavior would have triggered, to test out if my new insight is working.

If these scenarios come up, I will choose new small behaviors using an Implementation Intention (If...then... statement)

The Swish, softened

Swish Variation : 2) I use an NLP technique called a "Swish Pattern", but I will allow my old pattern to be there, while also holding my new pattern in my awareness. I feel what comes up somatically, and compare the differences between the future scenarios of my old and new patterns.

Parts integration, without pretending the conflict is solved

Parts Integration : I use this technique to ask my conflicting parts what they want, what they are afraid of, what their need is, and see if I can find a 3rd option that satisfies both parts needs, without either part dominating my behavior.

What I will not use NLP for

Here is a list of things I do not do with NLP :

I do not deny people's legitimate signals.

I do not tell people to override their fear.

I do not use NLP for memory retrieval.

I do not use NLP to manipulate other people or convince myself of my intuition.

I do not remove legitimate signals or medical symptoms.

I do not use NLP on people who are panicked, destabilized, manic, having a "psychosis-like state", or are too high/dissociated to reality test.

I do not use NLP to make people feel like they are spiritually inferior to me if they disagree with me.

I do not use covert commands in my language.

I do not use NLP with people when there isn't enough time (I create urgency for them).

I do not use NLP on people without their consent (the idea that "your subconscious will let me know if you want me to do this" is NOT consent).

I do not use NLP on people in a suggestible state (in trance, tired, attracted to me, feeling shame or grief, or chemically altered).

Here is a rough outline of the entire NLP process (though I rarely do all of this) :

Running the whole NLP sequence

Induce/Contain the person (get their attention or stabilize them).

Ask for their permission.

Get a representation of their pattern (image, feeling, size, color, location, movement, etc.).

Find out what that part/pattern is protecting for them.

Appendix H: Demons, jinn, hostile presences, and “Unattached Burdens”

I speak here from experience.

When you’re doing hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca-ing, going through a period of intense grief, praying, or whatever else may alter your consciousness, it’s possible you may run into something that you perceive to be a demon, a jinn, a parasitic energy, or whatever other dark entity or terrifying archetype you may encounter – it may be a voice or an image, and it does n’t just feel like an emotion or a younger part of you, but something that feels intrusive, hateful, seductive, mocking, etc.

First of all, it doesn’t matter if they’re demons or not. They may be literal demons, for all you know. Or they may be manifestations of your mind, burdens you’re carrying from previous relationships, whatever. What matters is what is the best way to deal with them.

Start with the room, the body, and basic safety

So what do you do when you encounter a demon, or a jinn, or something else that’s bad and intrusive?

First of all, do the usual things – make sure you’re not in danger from a medical standpoint, check your environment, check your body, make sure you’re not overstimulating yourself, make sure you’re not opening your mind too much. If you need to, open your eyes, ground yourself in your body and your environment, remove yourself from any bad influence you’re surrounding yourself with, stop stimulating your mind. Don’t go further into whatever it is you’re doing – don’t be curious, don’t try to figure out what it is.

Tell yourself, “If this can be integrated in this moment, it’s welcome. If not, it can wait until later. The adult part of me is always welcome, and so is my body.”

If you feel like you’re in any danger of doing anything harmful to yourself or others, if you feel like you’re going psychotic and you’re afraid of it, if you feel like you won’t be able to sleep when the self-hypnosis session is over, if you feel overly paranoid, if you feel physical pain in your chest, if you feel like you’re going to have a seizure, if you feel like you’re too hot in a bad way, if you feel like you’ve taken too much of something, if you feel like you won’t be able to function in the world anymore – then the self-hypnosis session is over, and you should get help in the “real world”.

A response check, not a verdict about what it is

If, however, you feel like you can deal with it, check in with yourself and see what’s best to do. Again, it doesn’t matter if it’s a demon or not. Put your hand on your heart, breathe comfortably, and check in with yourself about what to do in this situation.

Internalize the fact that you don’t have to know what it is. Find out if it helps to be warm towards it or to keep it at arm’s length. Keep in mind that you don’t have to do what it tells you to do.

If you feel vulnerable, if you feel tightness in your throat, if you feel sadness or fear or a need to protect yourself from it, call upon your Nurturer. If you don’t feel better, or if it continues being hostile towards you, stop trying to deal with it.

Internalize the fact that you don’t have to know where it comes from. Check in with yourself about whether or not this is helpful. You don’t have to find out if it’s a protector immediately, and you may not be able to comfort it quickly, but work with it as if it were, at least for now.

Do not fight from fear

Your first instinct may be to fight it, banish it, hate it, show it that you’re more powerful than it is, argue with it, panic, become your own lesser self in fear of it, etc. Some people may want to use traditional prayer or mantras or protection or banishing or exorcism techniques, and those may well work for them. But if you’re fighting it out of fear…

It only becomes a center of attention if you hate it and therefore give it a hook in you. (To counter pride, or to feel you must panic and defeat it.)

So the next time it comes up you can just say, “I see that there is no reason to hate and revile what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to merge with or become what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to obey what I am experiencing. I see that there is no reason to try to defeat what I am experiencing out of fear. I choose to return my attention to loving awareness.”

A bodily boundary: compassion present, door closed

This is especially important if the presence feels in any way hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, etc – if it doesn’t feel like it respects your boundaries. You don’t want to approach it with soft sentimental love in this case; you want to approach it with love but also maintain a boundary.

So, sit up, get grounded in your feet, straighten your spine, pull your shoulder blades back just slightly so that your chest is open but not exposed, feel the boundary of your skin all around your torso, feel the perimeter of your body, and simply say, “While I recognize that there may be suffering present here, I want all suffering to go back where it came from. The boundary of this skin is the boundary of an adult now. You don’t get to come in the house anymore.”

If it might be psychosis or destabilization

This is assuming that you are having a symbolic experience of “hostile presences” which responds to grounding and love. It may be that what you are experiencing is actually psychotic or a form of destabilization.

If you feel like you are under attack for multiple days at a time, if you are not able to sleep, if you are not able to function normally, if you are hearing voices telling you to do things, if you feel you need to hurt yourself or somebody else, if you feel you are going manic, if you feel you can’t communicate normally, if you feel you can’t distinguish between what you are experiencing symbolically and normal reality, get help immediately. It’s not something to deal with in hypnosis.

As a general rule, if this is making you more loving, more grounded, more relational, more honest, and more functional, then it’s probably OK to keep doing it gently. If it’s making you more Paranoid, more sleepless, more grandiose, more isolated, more scared, or more unreal, don’t go deeper, get help.

The cosmic-download humility test

Finally, presences, shadow forces, or grandiose parts may try to respond by giving you a sense that you’re special, trying to “download cosmic info” to you, try to give you a special mission, make you feel doing the dishes is beneath you, etc. You can just say, “Thank you for the imagery, but I don’t need your grand performance. Unless the info you’re trying to download to me can help me do the dishes, clean my room, be more honest, be more helpful, be more loving, keep my promises, take care of my body by resting and eating etc. I don’t need it.

Unless the “guidance” you’re trying to give me can help me be more beautiful, honest, relational, humble, useful, and take care of my dishes and my room, I don’t need it.”

Don’t become an entity hobbyist

Finally, some of you may be tempted to make this an area of hobbyism – to become interested in demons or jinns or hostile presences or Unattached Burdens or whatever. I just don’t want you to do that. They all lead to the same thing, which is how to maintain a presence of love while also making your mind harder to hook. Beyond that, I don’t want you to be hobbyists in this area.

Appendix J: A practical induction library

Practise! Work out in advance which one you want to do and what you want to use it for (pick just one) and whether or not you want to do it at all! Any of these ‘families’ of induction can be done as light inductions, with eyes open, or instead of trance you can just do them as a contact. Once you start an induction, you will want to notice what’s going on (even if nothing changes) and work out what to do next, move, imagine something else, change the sensory channel you’re using, do nothing, stop the induction sequence and do something else… . Whatever you do, make sure you bring yourself back to waking at the end of an induction.

NB: if you can’t ‘see’ the images you’re trying to visualise, that’s fine, change them into words, rhythm, spatial relations, something to touch or move or just plain ‘knowing’… .

Stretch and release

Stretch and Release: Work out what will be supporting you, focus on the feeling of support. You can also focus on where one of your hands or feet is. Either actually, or in your imagination, stretch a little bit, either stretching that part of your body slightly or pressing down into the support, and then let go of the effort, just relax. See if there is any difference, even if there isn’t. Do this for no more than 3 places on your body. Think of it as ‘releasing’ as you go through the sequence. Which bit of your body, or voice, needs this? What do you need to support it? Bring your body back to normal movement and return.

Supported floating

Supported Floating: Work out what is supporting you and where your weight is, imagine that the support is holding a tiny bit (1%) more of your effort. It’s like floating but you don’t have to lose contact, or just keep it at the same level, just enough weight/pressure. See what happens, you can fractionate this if you want, perhaps noticing your normal awareness when you breathe in and the support when you breathe out. Tell yourself you are going to do this before you do it. What can you hear more easily now? Bring yourself back to normal feeling of support and return.

Rhythmic breath or pulse

Rhythmic: Use your breathing or slightly hum in your throat to make a natural rhythm, or tap your finger or listen to sounds outside to make an artificial one. You can even do it by counting to yourself (silently) or with no rhythm at all. Tell yourself you are going to say “here, and here again” over and over, and notice what you pay attention to in between the phrases, then stop saying it. Notice what you become aware of in the first beat – you don’t need to make your mind blank, just notice what comes up. Does it make any words, feelings, needs or actions more clear? Bring back your normal rhythm and return.

Unwinding object

Unwinding Object: Good for when you have a few different strands to one thing you want to work on. Imagine an object unwinding – maybe some yarn, some bubbles, or some knots that you place beside you. Once you’ve placed them all, give yourself a minute to look at them all, you don’t have to change anything, but you can label them if you need to (just a word or two). How many did you put down? Which one do you need to work on, what does it need – warmth, protection, action? Keep one strand in your attention and put the others somewhere you can see them and return.

Sensory journey

Sensory Journey: Pay attention to the sounds in the room you’re in and how your body feels, then imagine yourself walking somewhere. Where do you want to go? Listen to the sounds of your footsteps and take in your surroundings as you walk, what do objects feel like if you touch them, what landmarks do you see? When you feel you have enough of your attention, imagine the scenery changing until you are in a place where you can talk to whoever you need to (or you can just cut to the chase, if you prefer). Pay attention to something without worrying about what it means. Allow yourself to be curious about what’s going to happen next, but don’t make it a “what are they going to do to you?” kind of thing. When you are ready to finish, imagine yourself walking back the way you came and close the space.

Gradual wave

Gradual wave: start with a very small neutral area, feel into it a little and then imagine a wave spreading out to a new area that is still ok. Sense into the new area (or continue using the old). See if there is anything that could use medical attention, and if you imagine it being fixed, what is different afterwards? Does the body want any contact, space, words, other care? Let the mental image go, sense your body, sense your contact points, come back.

Care workshop

Care workshop: prepare the workshop (time, place, tools, boundaries, etc). Invite the signal/feeling/young part to come as close as they want. Try to avoid any language that makes you not one person. Care for it as best you can, by asking what it wants and giving that if you can, or sensing into it and responding, or just being with it. Take breaks, get back in contact if that's ok, take more breaks, etc. Keep bringing in adult functions (or borrow someone else's function). Have the adult part of you run the show. Goal is to make it "good as you". Close the workspace, reassure yourself that you are one whole person, that you're an adult now, and come back.

Resource embodiment

Resource: pick a resource quality. Imagine yourself accessing 1% more of that quality (or just sense yourself). What is different? How is your body, voice, etc? Do this a few times to strengthen it. Come back, keeping the quality and one positive action that you would do with it, but leaving the "person" behind, saying "I am me".

No-trance inner contact

For the no trance inner contact, I would do: Pacing: notice you can see, it's (day of the week), you have feet, you can read, you can write, etc. Suggestion: in your mind, ask a question, but don't focus too hard. Choice: you can answer the question, write an answer, write that you don't know, take a break, rephrase the question, ask someone else, stop doing this, etc. Autonomous: write whatever you get. Deepener: none. Handoff: have your adult self answer the question in whatever way is appropriate, preferably by writing or doing. Integration/exit: reality test the autonomous, do something based on it, stop doing it.
